english: Shepherd, someone stole three oxen. Who found them? A known young man stole the cows of the gods. He bound leaves on their feet and they [the owners] searched for them. Did they catch the youth? They caught him; he sang them a song and they smiled. Now I am looking for leaves for the house. Search, and ask for a spear too.

english: Grandmother, why does the dog sleep at our hearth? It has earned it. Our cows slipped away in the snow. He went and searched for them all through the night. Did he find them? He found them at the river and drove them home. Did grandfather give him meat? He gave him meat. Now leave him be. Good dog.

Shepherd, why is the wolf hungry? Listen to the story. A hungry wolf met a dog. The dog said: come with me to a big house. Did he go? He went, and saw the dog tied at the door. Did he stay? He did not stay. Better a free wolf than a tied dog. May I be free.

Father, Dyeus is thundering. Why does he thunder? Perkunos is chasing the serpent. The serpent stole cattle and hid them under a rock/oak. Does Perkunos find him? He finds him. Now he strikes the oak. I am afraid of the thunder. Child, don't be afraid: Perkunos protects our house. May he kill the serpent. Listen. Now Dyeus falls silent.

english: Old man, tell me a story. How many cows did you drive off? As a young man I drove them. Ten men went at night. Weren't you afraid? My heart trembled. Then we moved the cows in the field. Did shepherds see you? A young man saw us and they were sleeping. Then we drove a hundred cows home. What did the king give you? He gave me an ox and great fame.

english: Father, is the wolf bad? Not every wolf is bad. Listen to the she-wolf story. The chief left his two sons at the river. Did the river carry them off? It did not. The she-wolf found them and gave them her milk. Did they grow up? They grew and built a great village. The she-wolf was good.
